thread:
maria: heads up — saw an Insights widget show rows from another org for ~2s during a rapid org switch :eyes:

maria: repro steps: switch org quickly via quick-switch (cmd+k) -> open Insights panel -> notice a flash of other org rows, then it refreshes to correct org

maria: putting logs below, grabbed request headers and response sampling:

maria: ```
GET /internal/console/widgets/insights?org_id=org-985
X-User: maria@redwood
X-Org: org-985
X-Prefetch-Key: qk-42

200 OK (cached: true)
payload.rows[0].org_id=org-110 (mismatch)
```

dan: ugh, looks like prefetch cache key isn't including workspace affinity header. could be a race between quick-switch navigation and the prefetch service returning the previous org's cached response

kaya: agree. I think the router sets X-Org for the initial navigation but the prefetch worker relies on cookie-based tenant lookup. fast switch means cookie hasn't updated yet -> stale prefetch hits

kaya: quick mitigation: disable prefetch for Insights widget for everyone behind rollout flag until we push a fix? that avoids cross-tenant flashes in UI while we triage

jordan: we have a rollout flag for prefetch at route-level already (route.prefetch.enabled). can flip it for the Insights route to false in staging and prod Canary 10% -> 100% if safe

ashwin: adding telemetry note — this produced a handful of cross-tenant metric samples. I'll tag the affected traces with span attribute "tenant_leak=true" so we can query them and check user impact

maria: thanks. to be clear, the leak only lasted a UI frame and wasn't persisted server-side, but still bad for PII-sensitive customers. we should treat it as an incident for compliance teams to review

dan: root cause hypothesis: cache key omitted org_id and user-session fingerprint on internal prefetch path. code path: services/prefetch/cache.js -> keyFor(req) only uses route+query+prefetch-key currently. suggested patch: include header X-Org (fall back to cookie) and session id

dan: patch sketch:

```js
function keyFor(req) {
  const org = req.headers['x-org'] || req.cookies['org'];
  const sid = req.cookies['session_id'] || req.headers['x-session-id'];
  return `${req.route}:${req.query.prefetchKey}:org=${org}:sid=${sid}`;
}
```

kaya: +1 but add defensive check for missing org -> treat as cache miss. we should also add a unit test that simulates rapid header/cookie flip and confirms no stale hits

sre-bot: deploys/team-deploy started deployment 1745553400 for services/prefetch@canary

maria: can we also add a server-side validation that rejects cached responses whose payload.org_id != evaluated org header before returning to client? double-checking on the server buys us extra safety if keys miss something

ashwin: good call. add a guard: if (payload.org_id && payload.org_id !== orgFromReq) { return cache.miss(); } and increment metric prefetched.response_org_mismatch

jordan: ops plan: 1) flip prefetch rollout for Insights to off (canary 10% rollback) 2) land cache key patch + payload guard 3) add unit + integration tests 4) re-enable prefetch route rollout 10% -> 100% 5) notify compliance w/ scoped telemetry query

maria: I'm going to open a short incident doc with timeline and put the affected customer/org ids (redacted) in the doc. will ping legal if we see persisted exposure. :(

dan: assigning to @kaya and @ashwin for code + telemetry. I'll take the rollback flip in the console rollout system. tagging @jordan for deploy coordination

kaya: grabbing it now, will push PR with tests. reassign to oncall if blocked

ashwin: I'll add the metric and the analytics query. also adding an alert that fires if prefetched.response_org_mismatch > 0 in 5m window so we catch regression

maria: thanks team. let's aim for a mitigated rollback in the next 30m and a PR review in the next 90m. :thumbsup:
